A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GoFlow research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated domain-randomization experiments, hyperparameter and range analyses, and real-world gear-insertion trials, including Figures 2–3 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation and robot experiments and adds threshold-sensitivity results in Figure 13 and lower-tail reward results in Table 3.

M1.justification: The PPO actor-critic, neural spline flow, entropy/KL objective, importance-sampling updates and belief-space planning procedures are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 retain the same steps despite relocation and formatting changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the illustrative 2D domains, Cartpole, Ant, Quadcopter, Quadruped, Humanoid, simulated gears and real-world gear manipulation. Humanoid is newly named in Section 5.1 but already appears in v1's Figure 3 and Appendix A.3.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain FullDR, NoDR, DORAEMON, LSDR and ADR. The new threshold and CVaR analyses reuse this comparator set. Newly cited adversarial and adaptation methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.7 adds evaluation across success thresholds from 0 to 1.2 times JT, and Table 3 introduces lower-tail CVaR using the 10th-percentile cutoff. Existing randomization bounds, episode horizons and training settings remain unchanged. The newly specified 4096 evaluation samples document an existing experiment.

E4.justification: v2 adds two substantive robustness questions across the six simulation tasks: dependence of coverage comparisons on the success threshold, and performance in the lower reward tail. Figure 13 and Table 3 provide these analyses; the existing hyperparameter sweeps, range study and planning case study remain.

E5.justification: Table 2 changes its uncertainty description from standard deviation to standard error and specifies a one-tailed z test at 0.05. However, Appendix A.9 retains the previous t-test and standard-deviation description, leaving the actual procedure unclear. Figure 3 still reports five seeds and standard-error bands; the new threshold study explicitly uses one seed.

E6.justification: Table 2 extensively revises reported values: GoFlow's Cartpole entry changes from 0.109 to 0.138 and Gears from 0.104 to 0.035. Figure 13 and Table 3 add threshold-dependent coverage and CVaR results. Figure 3's plotted values and Table 1's robot success counts remain unchanged. Table 2's conflicting reward/coverage descriptions prevent treating its revisions as established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, the belief-space definitions and Appendix A.2's importance-sampling derivations are retained. No assumptions, proofs or formal properties are added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion replace general statements that GoFlow outperforms other approaches with the more specific claim of higher domain coverage. The central methodological, sim-to-real and multi-step planning contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.7 interprets the comparative coverage advantage across varying thresholds while acknowledging that absolute coverage depends strongly on the threshold. Section 6.4 newly explains yaw invariance through the rotation-independent insertion success criterion. Existing limitations concerning flow instability and manually tuned planning thresholds remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the minimal-supplementary-code statement and conditional future release with a direct project-code link. Section 5.2 newly specifies 4096 uniformly sampled evaluation initializations, and Appendix A.3 explains threshold selection and qualitative verification. These additions improve documentation without establishing changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands its positioning, distinguishing adversarial randomization from curriculum approaches and contrasting GoFlow with methods requiring real-world feedback, retraining or strategy search. Eight added references also connect the planning application to task-directed exploration; these comparisons were absent from v1.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work passages are rewritten, evaluation explanations are expanded, and the appendix gains a threshold-analysis subsection and revised code-release heading. The overall narrative and main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 13 and Table 3, transposes Table 1, changes Figure 3's colors and legend order, and clarifies labels and captions in Figures 4–5. Appendix displays and algorithms are rearranged, with the old Figure 13 retained as Figure 14. Most existing visual content and design are preserved.

improvement.justification: The threshold sweep addresses dependence on the chosen success criterion, while CVaR results reveal limits to GoFlow's advantage beyond coverage. More precise claims, evaluation details and a code link improve transparency. These are limited gains: the threshold study uses one seed, and Table 2's reward/coverage, standard-error/deviation and z-test/t-test inconsistencies remain unresolved.
